column1: # Files worms plant in a project and run from a hook or a task when the folder is opened.
# One line each, tab separated. After editing, run: bash tools/gen.sh
#   folder    .claude or .vscode
#   file      the file's name
#   incident  an id from data/incidents.tsv
#   note      shown under the file when it is found. A settings file that runs any of these
#             files is shown with "runs" before the note (or a general line, if the notes differ)
#   alone     yes: only a worm uses this name, so the file counts wherever it is found. no: projects
#             use the name too, so the file counts only in a project that holds a yes file, or when
#             its SHA-256 is one in sha256; anywhere else section 2 lists it as a file to read
#   sha256    for a no file, the SHA-256 values the sources publish for it, separated by commas, or -.
#             A yes file counts on its name and carries - (gen.sh refuses a value): its published
#             values are given below
# Wiz on the TanStack wave: "Check .claude/ and .vscode/ directories for router_runtime.js or
# setup.mjs", and setup.mjs 2258284d. Socket on the keyv wave: .claude/math_init.js (SHA-256
# 9fc2570b7cef51c1b8df116d144d11ff4096357be7d2c4c6367cfc2509cf1bcc, the payload, identical to the npm
# packages' Math_Symbol.js), and setup.mjs fd3ca400 (the loader in .claude and .vscode, identical in
# both) and 54dc7ea5 (the loader in the npm packages). A hook counts when it runs any of these file
# names from either folder. The commit that planted the keyv files in its source repository
# (jaredwray/keyv d8c850c7) has math_init.js in .claude only, with the same setup.mjs in .claude and
# .vscode, so .vscode/math_init.js has no line: the loader there counts by its SHA-256, and a task that
# runs math_init.js from either folder counts.
# Wiz on April's Mini Shai-Hulud wave: the worm places .claude/execution.js, a copy of its payload
# identical to the npm packages' execution.js (eb6eb415 in @cap-js/postgres and @cap-js/db-service,
# 6f933d00 in @cap-js/sqlite, 80a3d287 in mbt), and setup.mjs 4066781f, its dropper, in .claude and
# .vscode, run by a SessionStart hook and a folder-open task. That wave's intercom-client renamed its
# payload router_runtime.js (StepSecurity), so these three are every payload the wave named
# execution.js; StepSecurity also publishes intercom-client's setup.mjs, fe646996 (the loader in the npm
# package), listed as the keyv packages' loader is. Projects name files execution.js too, so it counts
# only by those SHA-256 values or beside a worm's own file. Socket on lightning, that
# wave's PyPI release: its payload plants .claude/router_runtime.js, a copy of itself, with setup.mjs
# files beside it. It also commits .github/workflows/format-check.yml, a CI workflow, which has no line:
# a planted file sits in .claude or .vscode, and the home scan does not look in .github/workflows.
# SafeDep on the AntV wave: the worm commits .claude/index.js, a copy of its payload (SHA-256
# a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c, the npm packages' index.js), and
# setup.mjs in .claude and .vscode, run by a SessionStart hook and a folder-open task. Projects name
# files index.js too, so it counts only by that SHA-256 or beside a worm's own file. Its
# .github/workflows/codeql.yml, a CI workflow that dumps the repository's secrets, has no line: a
# planted file sits in .claude or .vscode, and the home scan does not look in .github/workflows.
